title: Regime Consistency of an Entropy-Gradient Coupling: Lyα, BAO and RSD Tests within a Structural Coherence Framework
description: Empirical regime-consistency test of an entropy-gradient coupling T(z) in Energy-Flow Cosmology across three independent probes: DESI Lyα P1D (z=3), BOSS DR12 BAO distances, and BOSS DR12 RSD growth. Using a single coupling calibrated near z≈0.5 and evaluated within the Structural Coherence Evaluation framework, the study finds a near-null Lyα effect, improved BAO fits, and marginally improved RSD, yielding a combined Δχ² ≈ −3.89 with one added parameter.

transition_kernel.description: Distance-coupling kernel that sets the redshift dependence of the entropy-gradient coupling.

transition_function.description: Normalized transition function peaking at unity; used to propagate a single coupling across redshift regimes.

modified_friedmann.description: Background modification used for BAO and RSD tests; late-time H(z) enhanced by a single parameter β scaled by T(a).

omega_m_of_z.description: Redshift evolution of the matter fraction used to compute g_D(z) and T(z) on a ΛCDM-calibrated background.

key_results.main_finding: A single T(z) calibrated near z≈0.5 yields regime-consistent predictions across Lyα P1D, BAO, and RSD without dataset-specific tuning.
datasets_used: BOSS DR12 BAO distances (Alam et al. 2017)

sealed_predictions.statement: At z = 3, Lyα P1D shows a near-null EFC effect with A·T(z) = α_L2·T(z) ≈ 0.037 (range ≈ 0.02–0.06 for α_L2 ±1σ), yielding amplitude and slope pulls < 0.5σ relative to ΛCDM.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Higher-precision DESI/WEAVE Lyα P1D measurements of Δ★ and n★ at z ≈ 3.

sealed_predictions.statement: At z ≈ 0.4–0.6, a single background parameter β > 0 produces correlated shifts that reduce ΛCDM’s DM overprediction and mildly suppress growth; BAO+RSD jointly prefer β ≈ 0.08 over β = 0.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: DESI DR2/DR3 BAO+RSD joint fits with full covariance and percent-level systematics control.

sealed_predictions.statement: At recombination (z ≈ 1100) the coupling vanishes, T(z) ≈ 10^-10, implying GR recovery and no detectable early-time deviations from ΛCDM background.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: CMB primary/secondary anisotropy and early-time expansion constraints (Planck, Simons Observatory, CMB-S4).

kill_criteria: KC1: DESI/WEAVE Lyα P1D at z ≈ 3 requires |A·T(z=3)| ≥ 0.08 at ≥5σ, incompatible with T(z)=0.107 and α_L2=0.34±0.16 (even α_L2=0.51 gives A·T≈0.055).
KC2: Joint BAO+RSD analysis with full covariance (e.g., DESI) returns β = 0.00 ± 0.02 (68% CL) and no improvement over ΛCDM (Δχ² ≥ 0), excluding β ≈ 0.08 at ≥3σ.
KC3: High-precision RSD at z = 0.5–0.7 robustly finds fσ8 higher than ΛCDM by ≥3σ, contradicting the EFC prediction of growth suppression from enhanced Hubble friction.
KC4: Early-Universe constraints demand a non-vanishing late-time coupling at z ≳ 1100, e.g., β·T(z=1100) ≥ 10^-4, violating the T(z) ∝ (1 − Ω_m(z)) suppression and GR recovery.
KC5: A single α_L2 calibrated at z ≈ 0.5, when propagated via T(z), leads to ≥3σ tension with either Lyα P1D or RSD in the tested redshift range, breaking regime consistency.

alpha_L2.description: EFC coupling amplitude from BOSS DR12

bao_boss_dr12.note: EFC corrects systematic ΛCDM DM overprediction

bao_rsd_combined.note: Δχ² = 3.84 corresponds to 95% CL for 1 DOF

sce_evaluation.summary: Neither framework dominates the full SCE profile. ΛCDM wins on raw compression; EFC wins on structural discipline.

forbidden_patterns.definition: If T(z=3)/T(peak) > 0.5 AND (|amplitude pull| > 3σ OR |slope pull| > 3σ), then regime-transition logic is inconsistent
If Boltzmann solver with μ(z) = 1 + A·T(z) produces CMB Cl residuals exceeding Planck error bars
If fσ₈ deviates > 3σ at any BOSS z while αL2 within ±2σ of best-fit
If β > 0 simultaneously worsens both BAO and fσ₈ vs ΛCDM
If β passes BAO+RSD but fails CMB lensing or SN Ia > 3σ

open_requirements: Full MCMC joint fit with proper covariance matrices between BAO and RSD
Self-consistent EFC background (T(z) currently uses ΛCDM Ωm(z))
Full Boltzmann CMB power spectrum calculation
key_conclusions: Single coupling function T(z) produces consistent predictions across three cosmological regimes
One-parameter modification (β = 0.08) simultaneously improves BAO and growth (Δχ² = −3.89)
High-z null prediction at z = 3 consistent with DESI Lyα P1D data
GR recovery at z = 1100 guaranteed by T(z) → 0 with margins > 10⁸
EFC shows higher Layer Consistency and lower Model Plasticity than ΛCDM
Neither framework dominates full SCE structural profile
